Senior Frontend Engineer — Kastell GmbH, Berlin Mitte.

About the role: you'll own the customer-facing web surface end to end, working alongside two backend engineers and a designer. Requirements: 5+ years with React, strong TypeScript, comfort with design systems, and a track record of shipping. We work from our Mitte office four days a week; Fridays are flexible. Compensation is competitive and reviewed annually.
Evaluated Kastell GmbH against your saved preferences.

s_onsite_rejects.content: That's a fair read on both. The frustrating part is that the work itself is close to what I want in each case — small product group, real ownership of the surface, TypeScript throughout. It's only the office pattern that rules them out, and both postings bury it near the bottom.

That pattern is worth naming: both postings lead with autonomy and craft and defer the attendance requirement to the last line. I'll keep surfacing the working pattern in the first two criteria from now on so it never reads as a footnote in an evaluation.

Please do. And while we're here — I'd rather not look at agencies or consultancies at all. I've done two years of that and the work is always someone else's roadmap. Product companies where the engineers are close to the customer is what I'm after, even if the brand is smaller.

Noted as a preference rather than a dealbreaker, since you framed it as "rather not" — I'll weight agency and consultancy postings down but still show them if everything else is unusually strong. If you'd prefer them filtered out entirely, say so and I'll move it up to a must-have.

Preference is right for now. One more thing on the office question — I'm not against meeting people. A quarterly offsite or an occasional team week is fine and I'd probably enjoy it. What I can't do is a standing weekly commute. So the rule is about recurring attendance, not about ever being in a room together.

That's a useful distinction and I've recorded it that way: the constraint is on recurring attendance, not on travel. A role advertising a quarterly gathering won't be flagged; one advertising "two days a week in office" will be, regardless of how it is labelled.
Both of those are onsite 4 days, so I've ruled them out — let's not look at anything that needs more than one office day a month.

memoryEffects.label: Saved to memory — Avoids onsite roles

s_onsite_rejects.content: Understood — one office day a month is now the hard ceiling. Paste the next description whenever you're ready and I'll check it against that first.

s_platform_eng.content:
Different shape this time — platform rather than product.

Staff Platform Engineer — Vireo Labs, remote within the EU.

About the role: you will own the internal developer platform used by roughly ninety engineers. Requirements: deep Node and TypeScript, Next.js at scale, build tooling, observability, and a bias toward paved roads over gatekeeping. Responsibilities include the component library, the CI pipeline, release tooling, and a shared on-call rotation with the infrastructure group. Fully remote across the EU. Band: €98,000–€118,000 plus equity.
Evaluated Vireo Labs against your saved preferences.

s_platform_eng.content: The on-call line is the sticking point, yes. Worth adding that I've led an accessibility remediation programme across a component library — WCAG 2.2 AA — so platform work of that kind isn't unfamiliar. It just can't come with a pager.

Recorded the accessibility programme as a skill. On the rotation: some platform groups run business-hours-only support with infrastructure taking the overnight pages. That is a reasonable thing to ask in a first conversation rather than screening the role out on the posting alone.
Agreed. One more preference while I think of it: async-first written culture, with meetings clustered into a couple of days rather than scattered across the week.

Saved as a preference. It's rarely stated outright in a posting, so I'll infer it from signals — a public handbook, written RFCs, published timezone spread — and mark it partial rather than matched when the evidence is thin, as it was here.
That's the right call. Make the on-call point a hard one though — no paging rotation outside business hours, full stop. I've done three years of it and I'm not going back.

s_platform_eng.content: Stored as a dealbreaker alongside the onsite rule. Vireo now reads as not-recommended unless they confirm platform engineers sit outside the paging rotation.

Of the four roles in your sessions so far, one published a band. I mark a withheld band partial rather than mismatched — it isn't evidence against the role, only an absence of evidence for it.
That's the right treatment. Keep the floor pinned so it shows at the top of memory.
Pinned. The €95,000 floor will now lead the compensation group in long-term memory and be cited in every evaluation that touches pay.
